_guide.what this file is: The schema for an exercise, with a worked example below it. Copy this file, replace the example with your topic, and it is a valid spec.
_guide.how it becomes a page: The object from "meta" down is pasted into the <script type="application/json" id="spec"> data island inside assets/exercise.html. Keys starting with _ are ignored by the page; keep or delete them.
_guide.meta.title: What the student sees as the page heading. Plain, specific, no marketing.
_guide.meta.slug: Lowercase repo and folder name: letters, digits, hyphens. It becomes the GitHub repo name and therefore the URL.
_guide.meta.goal: One sentence starting 'After this you can ...'. The one capability the exercise trains. See rule 8 in references/learning-science.md.
_guide.meta.minutes: Honest length of one sitting. 6 to 12 steps fits a 10 minute phone session (rule 12).
_guide.meta.criterion.text: The bar in the student's words, shown on the intro and results screens (rule 10).
_guide.meta.criterion.minCorrect: Number of steps that must be right for the criterion to count as met. Keep it in agreement with the text.
_guide.steps[].id: Short stable id used in the results list. Any unique string.
_guide.steps[].tag: Sub-topic of this step. Used to interleave different sub-topics instead of blocking them (rule 5).
_guide.steps[].kind: "choice" (tap one option) or "short" (type the answer from memory). Mix them.
_guide.steps[].prompt: The question. It must never contain or hint at the answer (rule 1).
_guide.steps[].options: Required for "choice": 3 to 5 short options, each a plausible answer. Order them so the right one is not always in the same position.
_guide.steps[].answer: For "choice": the zero-based index of the right option. For "short": a string, or an array of accepted strings. Matching is lowercase, whitespace-collapsed, and trailing punctuation is ignored.
_guide.steps[].feedback: Why the answer is right. Shown after every attempt, right or wrong. Explain the mechanism, not the verdict (rule 2).
_guide.steps[].misconception: The tempting wrong belief and why it fails. Either one string, or an object keyed by wrong option index with a "default" fallback. Shown only after a wrong attempt (rule 3).
_guide.steps[].hint: Optional. One nudge, shown behind a Hint button. Put hints on early steps only, then drop them (rule 6).

meta.title: HTTP status codes
meta.goal: After this you can tell what went wrong in a request by reading its status code.

criterion.text: Get at least 4 of 5 right, including the 401 vs 403 pair.

steps.prompt: A request needs a login and did not send one. Which status comes back?
steps.feedback: 401 means the request carried no usable credentials, so the server is saying who are you. 403 means it knows who you are and still refuses.

misconception.1: 403 is the tempting pick because it sounds more severe, but 403 means the server recognized you and denied you. No credentials at all is 401.
misconception.3: 500 means the server broke. Nothing broke here; the request simply arrived without a login.

steps.hint: One of these two codes is about identity and the other is about permission.

steps.prompt: Name the one status family that means the request was fine and the server failed while handling it.
steps.feedback: 5xx is the server's own admission of fault. Anything 4xx blames the request.
steps.misconception: Most students answer 4xx. 4xx means the request was wrong; 5xx means the request was fine and the server could not finish the job.

steps.prompt: You are logged in and you ask for another user's billing page. The server has never offered you that page. Which status is closest to correct?
steps.feedback: You are known (so not 401) and the server refuses the action (403). Returning 200 with an empty page hides the refusal, and a redirect does not explain it.

misconception.1: 401 again means no credentials. You have credentials; they just do not grant this resource.
misconception.2: A 200 with nothing in it teaches the client nothing and hides a real authorization decision.

steps.prompt: A client sends JSON the server cannot parse. No server code ran. Which status fits?
steps.feedback: 400 is the client's fault: the bytes that arrived were malformed, so the server could not start work on them.

misconception.1: 500 means code ran and failed. Here the server rejected the payload before running anything.

steps.prompt: A status code comes back after a crash in your own handler. Write it.
steps.feedback: 500, or a more specific 5xx, is the server reporting that the request was fine and handling it was not.
